metadata.title: Density Pass 29 -- Louisiana Tigers Assault on Cemetery Hill (Ticks 318-332)
metadata.description: Hays's and Avery's Confederate brigades assault Cemetery Hill at dusk on July 2, briefly overrun the Union artillery, and are then driven back in hand-to-hand fighting. The only Confederate force to temporarily capture a position on Cemetery Hill. Avery mortally wounded writing his last note. The 'Tigers' rampage through the guns before Carroll's Union brigade countercharges.

placements.notes: Hays's Louisiana Tigers -- waiting for dark to assault Cemetery Hill. These are some of the roughest men in the Confederate army.
Avery's NC brigade -- assaulting alongside Hays. Avery is already wounded from an earlier action.
Wiedrich's Battery I and Ricketts's batteries on East Cemetery Hill -- about to be overrun
XI Corps on Cemetery Hill -- Krzyznowski and Schurz holding the north face
Louisiana Tigers CHARGING -- moving up the steep slope of Cemetery Hill in the fading light
Avery's NC brigade charging the northern face -- Avery falls from his horse, mortally wounded
Wiedrich's gunners fighting with rammers and handspikes -- Confederates are at the muzzles
Tigers IN THE GUNS -- overrunning Wiedrich's battery. Hand-to-hand at the cannon muzzles.
Avery's brigade reaching the crest -- but Avery is down, writing his last note on a scrap of paper with his blood: It was my fault.
Carroll's II Corps brigade COUNTERCHARGING -- Hancock has sent them at the double-quick
Union reinforcements hitting the Tigers from multiple directions
Louisiana Tigers repulsed -- Carroll's countercharge drives them off the hill. They held the guns for 10 minutes.
Avery's brigade retreating -- Avery lying in the field. His note: It was my fault. It was not.
Carroll's brigade holding Cemetery Hill -- the guns are retaken
Wiedrich's battery back in Union hands -- some guns spiked, others recovered intact
Louisiana Tigers reforming north of town -- 695 casualties from the assault. They came closest of any Confederates to holding Cemetery Hill.
